chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayyub and Hammad ibn Isa, all from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you have completed your Sa'y and you are in the state of Tamattu', then shorten your hair from its sides and your beard, and take (clip) from your moustache, and trim your nails, and leave some of them for your Hajj. And when you do that, you have become permitted from everything from which the one in Ihram is freed, and you have become prohibited from it. So perform Tawaf around the House voluntarily as much as you wish.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram: The sacred state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.سَعْي: Sa'y: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.طُوفْ: Tawaf: The ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّع: Mutamatti': A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the specific grooming actions required to end Ihram for Tamattu' Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith details the specific grooming acts—trimming hair, beard, mustache, and nails—that constitute the 'Qasr' (shortening) required to exit the state of Ihram after Sa'y for a Mutamatti' pilgrim. Scholarly tradition emphasizes that these actions serve as the definitive marker for the termination of Ihram restrictions, thereby permitting the performance of voluntary Tawaf and the resumption of normal marital and worldly activities.
